messages:
alex: Filing this here because a few customers hit RN/Expo with our SDK. Metro fails on ESM + node-shim imports (stream/crypto). Error: "Unable to resolve module 'stream' from .../dist/index.mjs".
rina: Are they on Expo Go or a custom dev client? Expo Go lacks some native random APIs.
marie: Metro doesn't respect conditional exports like Node does. We should provide a react-native entry (package.json "react-native": "dist/rn/index.js") and a small CJS fallback ("main") so older bundlers don't break.
sam: Agreed. For the RN bundle we can replace Node streams with a tiny async-iterator-based streamer (we only need token-by-token yields). That avoids pulling in full stream-browserify.
jess: Another runtime gotcha: AbortController and fetch behavior. React Native's global fetch historically doesn't support AbortController reliably. Our auth/retry code uses AbortSignal for timeouts. We need a runtime check and lightweight polyfill (abortcontroller-polyfill/dist/polyfill) in the RN entry. Example: `if (!global.AbortController) require('abortcontroller-polyfill/dist/polyfill')`.
alex: Right — saw reproducible hangs when retry backoff used signal.raise. Also RN fetch behaves differently for 401 flows; token refresh flows must not rely on service-worker style redirects.
rina: RNG is also tricky: Hermes sometimes doesn't expose crypto.getRandomValues. Suggest runtime fallback to expo-random or react-native-get-random-values: `if (!globalThis.crypto?.getRandomValues) require('react-native-get-random-values')`. Document the Expo Go caveat: recommend custom dev client for most stable native APIs.
marie: TS typing pain: our d.ts currently references NodeJS Readable and Buffer. RN projects without `dom` libs error. Two options: 1) ship a small ambient `rn-ambient.d.ts` in dist/rn that declares minimal globals (ReadableStream, crypto), or 2) update docs with TS config snippet: `{"compilerOptions": {"lib": ["es2020","dom"]}}`. I prefer 1 so customers don't touch tsconfig.
sam: For streaming API types we can provide narrower interfaces (AsyncIterable<string> rather than Node.Readable) which is cross-platform. That will simplify overloads.
jess: CI plan: add an integration pipeline that runs `expo prebuild && eas build --local` or at least `expo-cli r -c && metro bundler` against the sample app to catch bundling regressions. Also include a tiny sample Expo app in /examples/expo-sdk-quickstart.
alex: Can we also audit our bundle for accidental Node polyfills (util, process) that bloat metro bundles? Keep RN entry minimal and tree-shake friendly.
rina: Yep — use rollup/tsup target with replace plugin to stub Node-only modules and a small runtime shim for crypto/abortcontroller.
marie: Docs checklist for the PR: package.json fields (react-native/main/module), quick metro.config snippet for extraNodeModules (only as emergency), RN entry build script, RNG and AbortController runtime fallbacks, TS ambient d.ts, and sample Expo quickstart with notes about Expo Go vs custom dev clients.
sam: I'll prototype the dist/rn build and share bundle size + minimal shim code.
jess: I'll own the RFC + docs PR and add the Expo sample to CI. Also will include a short snippet showing how to detect runtime and require fallbacks.
dev-bot: RFC #248 updated: sdk-rn-entrypoints assigned to @jess, due in 5d.
alex: Thanks — want to avoid surprising early adopters with cryptic bundler errors.
